title: ACE Platform Architecture Tour
description: A guided walkthrough of the ACE (Autonomous Capability Enhancement) platform — a hosted 'Playbooks as a Service' system built on a three-agent architecture with FastAPI, MCP, Celery workers, and a React dashboard.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Python and TypeScript
Familiarity with REST APIs and async processing

steps.title: Project Overview
steps.description: Welcome to the ACE Platform! This is a hosted 'Playbooks as a Service' system that uses three AI agents (Generator, Reflector, Curator) to create self-improving instructions. The codebase is organized into four main areas: ace_core (the AI algorithm), ace_platform (the backend services), web (the React dashboard), and tests (comprehensive test suite). Configuration lives at the root with Docker, Fly.io deployment, and Alembic migrations.

interactiveActions.description: Explore the top-level directories to get a sense of the project layout

steps.title: ACE Core: The Three-Agent System
steps.description:
The heart of ACE is a three-agent architecture for self-improving AI instructions:

- **Generator** (generator.py): Produces reasoning trajectories for new tasks, surfacing strategies and pitfalls.
- **Reflector** (reflector.py): Analyzes execution outcomes and extracts insights with helpful/harmful counters.
- **Curator** (curator.py): Merges insights into structured playbook delta updates with de-duplication.

The orchestration happens in ace.py, which coordinates all three agents. The finance/ directory contains a domain-specific implementation for testing the ACE algorithm on financial NER tasks.

interactiveActions.description: Click on ace.py to see how the three agents are orchestrated

steps.title: Platform API: FastAPI Backend
steps.description:
The API layer is built with FastAPI and serves as the primary interface for the dashboard and external clients. Key routes include:

- **auth.py**: Login, signup, OAuth (Google/GitHub), password reset, email verification
- **playbooks.py**: Full CRUD for playbooks with versioning and outcome recording
- **evolutions.py**: Trigger evolution jobs and check status
- **api_keys.py**: Create and manage API keys for MCP clients
- **billing.py**: Stripe integration (feature-flagged)

The main.py file initializes the FastAPI app with middleware for CORS, rate limiting, and structured logging.

interactiveActions.description: Hover over the routes directory to see all API endpoints

steps.title: MCP Server: AI Tool Integration
steps.description:
The MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposes ACE capabilities as tools that AI assistants like Claude can call directly. It provides five core tools:

1. **list_playbooks()** — Browse available playbooks with semantic search
2. **get_playbook()** — Retrieve full playbook content
3. **create_playbook()** — Create new playbooks
4. **report_outcome()** — Record task execution results
5. **trigger_evolution()** — Kick off the three-agent evolution process

The server is mounted within the FastAPI app at /mcp and also supports standalone stdio transport for Claude Desktop.

interactiveActions.description: Click on server.py to see the MCP tool definitions

steps.title: Core Services: Business Logic
steps.description:
The core/ directory contains the business logic that powers the platform. Key services include:

- **playbooks.py**: PlaybookService — CRUD, versioning, and outcome management
- **evolution.py**: EvolutionService — wraps the ace_core three-agent system
- **auth.py / oauth_service.py**: JWT authentication and Google/GitHub OAuth
- **api_keys.py**: API key generation with bcrypt hashing and scoped permissions
- **llm_proxy.py**: MeteredLLMClient — OpenAI wrapper with usage tracking
- **metering.py**: Token counting and cost calculation
- **billing.py**: Stripe customer/subscription management
- **config.py**: Pydantic Settings for all environment variables

interactiveActions.description: Click playbooks.py to see the central PlaybookService

steps.title: Database & Background Workers
steps.description:
The data layer uses PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy ORM models (async via asyncpg for the API, sync via psycopg2 for workers). Key models: User, Playbook, PlaybookVersion, Outcome, EvolutionJob, UsageRecord, ApiKey.

Background processing uses Celery with Redis as the broker:
- **evolution_task.py**: Runs the three-agent evolution pipeline asynchronously
- **auto_evolution.py**: Triggers evolution automatically when 5+ outcomes accumulate
- **celery_app.py**: Task registry and Redis broker configuration

Concurrency is controlled via a UNIQUE index on (playbook_id) WHERE status IN ('queued', 'running') and SELECT FOR UPDATE row-level locking.

interactiveActions.description: Hover over the db directory to see ORM models and migrations

steps.title: Frontend: React Dashboard
steps.description:
The web dashboard is built with React 19, TypeScript, and Vite. It provides a full-featured UI for managing playbooks, viewing evolution history, and monitoring usage.

Key areas in src/:
- **pages/**: 23+ routes including Dashboard, PlaybookDetail, Auth, Admin, Billing, Settings
- **components/**: Reusable UI (PlaybookRenderer, OAuthButtons, SubscriptionGate, Layout)
- **contexts/**: React Context for auth state and theming
- **lib/**: API client (Axios), custom hooks, and utility functions

The app uses React Router for navigation, TanStack Query for server state, and Sentry for error tracking.

interactiveActions.description: Click App.tsx to see the route definitions

steps.title: Testing & Quality
steps.description:
The project has a comprehensive test suite with 54+ test files covering every layer. Notable tests:

- **test_mcp_server.py** (97KB): Exhaustive MCP tool testing
- **test_e2e_full_flow.py** (27KB): End-to-end user journey from signup to evolution
- **test_playbook_routes.py** (36KB): Playbook CRUD and versioning
- **test_e2e_billing_flow.py** (26KB): Complete Stripe billing lifecycle

Tests run with pytest. CI/CD is handled by GitHub Actions — push to main auto-deploys to staging, production requires manual trigger.

interactiveActions.description: Click conftest.py to see the shared test fixtures

steps.title: The Full Picture
steps.description:
Here's how it all connects:

1. **Users** interact via the React dashboard (web/) or AI assistants via the MCP server
2. **API requests** flow through FastAPI routes → core services → PostgreSQL
3. **MCP tool calls** (list, get, create playbooks, report outcomes) are authenticated via API keys
4. **Outcomes accumulate** — when 5+ outcomes exist, Celery auto-triggers evolution
5. **Evolution** runs the three-agent pipeline (Generator → Reflector → Curator) asynchronously
6. **New playbook versions** are created with the merged insights, improving future AI performance

Deployment: Docker Compose locally, Fly.io in production with separate staging/production environments. CI/CD via GitHub Actions.

interactiveActions.description: Explore freely — you now know the full architecture!
